content:
We have mass spec data: main peak at m/z 276.06655534899 (intensity 100). Likely molecular ion [M+H]+? Usually ESI positive mode gives [M+H]+. So molecular weight ~275.066? Actually if m/z is 276.0666 for [M+H]+, then neutral M = 275.058? Wait subtract 1.0073 => 275.0593. So molecular weight ~275.06 Da.

We need to deduce SMILES. Need more data: maybe we can get 13C NMR, 1H NMR, IR. But we want efficient minimal experiments. Could try to get formula via isotopic pattern? The isotopic distribution shows peaks at +1, +2 etc. The pattern: intensities: 100, 16.1, 33.6, 5.27, 0.53, 0.04... This pattern suggests presence of chlorine? Chlorine gives M+2 ~ 1/3 intensity. Here M+2 (278) intensity 33.6% relative to M (100). That's about 1/3, consistent with one chlorine (Cl-35/Cl-37 ratio ~3:1). Also M+1 (277) intensity 16% (C13 natural abundance ~1.1% per carbon). For a molecule with many carbons, M+1 would be higher. But 16% suggests maybe ~14 carbons? Actually M+1 intensity approx 0.011 * number of C + contributions from other elements (H, N, etc). 16% => 0.16 = 0.011*C => C≈14.5. So about 14-15 carbons. M+2 intensity 33% suggests one Cl (Cl-35 75.8%, Cl-37 24.2% => M+2 about 0.32 of M). Good.

Thus formula likely includes one Cl. Also maybe some O, N.

We can compute approximate formula: Let’s assume C14H?ClO? etc. Use exact mass: 276.066555 (M+H). Subtract H (1.007825) gives neutral mass 275.05873. Let's compute possible formula with one Cl (35.45). Use monoisotopic masses: C 12.0000, H 1.007825, N 14.003074, O 15.994915, Cl 34.968853 (Cl-35). So we need sum = 275.05873.

Let’s try C14H?ClO?:

C14 = 168.0
Cl = 34.9689 => total 202.9689
Remaining mass = 275.05873 - 202.9689 = 72.08983

Now O mass 15.9949 each. Try O2 = 31.9898 => remaining 40.1000. That could be H40? Too many H. H count = remaining /1.007825 ≈ 39.8 unrealistic.

Try O3 = 47.9847 => remaining 24.1051 => H ~23.9 => plausible H23. So formula C14H24ClO3? Let's compute exact: C14 (168) + H24 (24.1878) + Cl (34.9689) + O3 (47.9847) = 275.1414, a bit high (0.0827). Need lower H maybe 22? H22 mass = 22.17215. Sum = 168+22.172+34.969+47.985=273.126, too low.

Let's try C13: C13 = 156.0. Add Cl 34.969 = 190.969. Remaining 84.0897. O3 = 47.985 => remaining 36.1047 => H ~35.8 unrealistic. O4 = 63.9797 => remaining 20.11 => H~19.94. So C13H20ClO4? Compute: C13 156 + H20 20.1565 =176.1565; +Cl 34.969 =211.1255; +O4 63.9797 =275.1052 close (0.0465 high). Slight adjust H19: H19 mass 19.1487 => total 274.0974 low.

Try C12: C12=144. +Cl=34.969 =>178.969. Remaining 96.0897. O4=63.98 => remaining 32.11 => H~31.8 unrealistic.

Thus maybe there are also N atoms which affect mass.

Let's try formula with N: N mass 14.0031.

Assume C13H?ClN?O?. Let's try C13 (156) + Cl (34.969) =190.969. Add N (14.003) =204.972. Remaining 70.0867. O2 =31.9898 => remaining 38.0969 => H~37.8 unrealistic. O3 =47.985 => remaining 22.1017 => H~21.9 plausible. So C13H22ClNO3? Compute: C13 156 + H22 22.172 =178.172; +Cl 34.969 =213.141; +N 14.003 =227.144; +O3 47.985 =275.129, high by 0.07.

Try H20: C13H20ClNO3: H20 mass 20.1565 => total 156+20.1565=176.1565; +Cl 34.969=211.1255; +N 14.003=225.1285; +O3 47.985=273.1135 low.

Try O2 instead of O3: C13H22ClNO2: O2 mass 31.9898 => total 156+22.172=178.172; +Cl 34.969=213.141; +N 14.003=227.144; +O2 31.99=259.134 low.

Thus maybe formula C14H?ClN?O?. Let's try C14 (168) + Cl 34.969 =202.969. Add N 14.003 =216.972. Remaining 58.0867. O2 =31.99 => remaining 26.097 => H~25.9 plausible. So C14H26ClNO2? Compute: C14 168 + H26 26.2035 =194.2035; +Cl 34.969 =229.1725; +N 14.003 =243.1755; +O2 31.9898 =275.1653 high 0.1066.

Try H24: C14H24ClNO2: H24 mass 24.1878 => total 168+24.188=192.188; +Cl 34.969=227.157; +N 14.003=241.160; +O2 31.99=273.150 low.

Try O3: C14H24ClNO3: add O3 47.985 => total 275.142 low? compute: 168+24.188=192.188; +Cl 34.969=227.157; +N 14.003=241.160; +O3 47.985=289.145? Wait miscalc: 241.160+47.985=289.145 too high. Actually we need 275.059. So O3 too many.

Thus maybe no N, just C, H, O, Cl.

Try C15: C15=180 +Cl=34.969 =>214.969. Remaining 60.0897. O2=31.99 =>28.0997 => H~27.9 plausible. So C15H28ClO2? Compute: C15 180 + H28 28.2191 =208.219; +Cl 34.969=243.188; +O2 31.99=275.178 high 0.119.

Try H26: C15H26ClO2: H26 mass 26.2035 => total 180+26.2035=206.2035; +Cl 34.969=241.1725; +O2 31.99=273.1625 low.

Try O3: C15H26ClO3: add O3 47.985 =>321? Wait 241.1725+47.985=289.1575 high.

Thus maybe formula includes Br? But isotopic pattern suggests Cl.

The M+2 intensity 33% matches one Cl. Good.

Now we need SMILES. Could be a chlorinated aromatic compound with some substituents.

Mass 276 (M+H) suggests maybe chlorobenzene derivative with additional groups.

Chlorobenzene (C6H5Cl) mass = 112.0? Actually C6H5Cl monoisotopic mass: C6 72, H5 5.039, Cl 34.969 = 112.008. Too low.

Add maybe phenyl acetate etc.

Consider compound: 4-chlorobenzyl acetate? Let's compute: C9H9ClO2? Actually benzyl acetate: C9H10O2 (C9H10O2) mass 150.07. Add Cl => C9H9ClO2? mass 184? Not 276.

Maybe a chlorinated phenylpropanoic acid etc.

Let's compute formula C14H19ClO2? mass: C14 168, H19 19.149, Cl 34.969, O2 31.99 =254.108 low.

C14H19ClO3: add O3 47.985 => 270.103 low.

C14H19ClO4: add O4 63.98 => 286.09 high.

Thus maybe C15H21ClO2? C15 180 + H21 21.164 =201.164; +Cl 34.969=236.133; +O2 31.99=268.123 low.

C16H23ClO2: C16 192 + H23 23.179 =215.179; +Cl 34.969=250.148; +O2 31.99=282.138 high.

Thus maybe formula includes N as well.

Let's compute DBE using formula guess. But maybe we should get NMR to narrow.

We can request 1H NMR to see aromatic signals etc. That will help.

Let's call proton_nmr_spectra.
